title: Model admission, plugin registration, and serving launch recipes

sources.notes: Top-level shell baseline has no named functions. It validates its separate vLLM/CUDA installation, prepares CUDA pip-layout aliases, then execs a non-plugin RTX Pro 6000 r15 server; modeled as a direct external recipe boundary.
Top-level shell recipe has no named functions. It supplies the split-88B int4 admission modes and direct 32K/MNBT-256 launch contract.
Top-level shell recipe has no named functions. It supplies the 128K int4 launch and environment-sensitive B70 max-batch precedence; tensor execution is abstract.
Top-level profiling recipe has no named functions. It is modeled as direct exec with attribution-only profiling settings, not as performance evidence or a health gate.
Top-level dual-B70 recipe has no named functions. It supplies the 99B CausalLM/NVFP4 mode, bank repetition, BDF selector order, and environment-overridable direct launch.

Top-level older Track A recipe has no named functions. Its direct 35B launch is modeled; the chapter reports that its default phase1/phase7 paths do not match the checkout's src/phase1/src/phase7 layout.

Top-level tracked recipe has no named functions. It owns current r15 defaults, named-environment precedence, appended SB_EXTRA_ARGS, 95/75 remote placement, executable MNBT 2048, and optional speculative CLI.
Top-level direct recipe has no named functions. It supplies Laguna r20 47-row topology assumptions and explicitly inferred MNBT-512 launch defaults.
Declarative TOML has no code symbols. It exposes shooting_brake_vllm:register from the phase4 source tree and defines the root package/dependency boundary.
Card alias/BDF resolution, sysfs frequency and power operations are inventoried as pre-launch hardware state; they are not folded into plugin admission or claimed to schedule requests.

Top-level shell entrypoint has no named functions. The launch model covers process replacement, wrapper/recipe/trailing-argument precedence, health timeout, inspection, smoke, and the non-errexit READY edge.
Declarative TOML has no code symbols. It is the narrower shooting-brake-vllm packaging surface and registers shooting_brake_vllm:register against vLLM 0.26.0.

Mode-gated ordered patch installation and conflicting OOT replacement behavior are modeled. Patch internals beyond their admission/order conditions are explained but delegated to their owning subsystems.

Authoritative supported-model, bank identity/topology, text-only, rank/EPLB, alignment, int4 opt-in and exact per-device ownership admission. Binary byte layout and placement generation are referenced dependencies.

assumptions: The finite Profile and Architecture values stand for registry families; scenarios carry concrete hidden, layer, expert, top-k, and intermediate dimensions compared by modelContract.
BankStatus collapses header parsing, model identity, per-card coverage agreement, and explicit int4 ownership while preserving every represented accept/reject class.
The launch health counter is bounded to two failed polls instead of modeling wall-clock seconds; timeout ordering is preserved.
Trailing duplicate vLLM CLI options are modeled as the effective candidate because SB_EXTRA_ARGS is appended last; final duplicate-option semantics remain an external vLLM argparse boundary.
HTTP, JSON parsing, process signaling, oneAPI, sysfs, and accelerator work are external outcomes; the models do not assert their availability.
The plugin does not own vLLM request scheduling; MNBT/MNS are launch configuration observations only.
Comments and banner text are explanatory observations, never configuration inputs; source-visible mismatches remain explicit witnesses.

implementation_checks.description: CPU-call the registry lookup for all six repo IDs, one HF snapshot-form path, and an unknown ID; compare success/failure with registryMember and UnsupportedModel scenarios.

Use the existing CPU-only fake config/header fixtures to vary exact geometry, text-only state, TP/PP, EPLB, absent/wrong banks, and int4 opt-in; compare each outcome with qualify/rejectModel/rejectBank/rejectMode.
CPU-enumerate small CUDA/card/bank ID sets and compare exact coverage, overlap, cross-device duplication, gap, and extra-ID outcomes with the BadBank abstraction.

Source-inspect or isolate the OOT registry with empty, identical, and foreign entries; compare installed/idempotent/conflict outcomes and verify file overrides are unreachable when phase4_enabled is false.

CPU-parse the exported environment and final exec arguments under empty, named SB_MNBT, and duplicate SB_EXTRA_ARGS inputs; confirm executable default 2048, 95/75 placement, and trailing argument order independently of comments.

Run in an isolated CPU shell with controlled fake process/HTTP utilities to compare health success, bounded timeout, valid smoke, and failed command-substitution smoke; confirm timeout exits while a post-health smoke failure can still reach the banner.
